title: Everything Is an Optimisation Problem — Including Your CX Strategy

paragraphs.speaker: Eslam
paragraphs.text: Welcome to another episode of The CX Algorithm podcast. I'm Dr Eslam Afifi. Today's episode is a bit of a special one. And the reason for that is optimization is a word that we have been hearing for the last two to three months. With everything going around the world right now, with all the energy crisis that we have in different parts of the world. I thought this is a great case study that we can learn a lot from, especially as a CX practitioner. Optimization is every single meeting to report, or even, or even sometimes on what we call quarterly meetings that we have with our counterparts across the organization. It's something that we always have to think of. And really, I have the pleasure today to host one of the people that inspired me when I spoke to him the first time. We met the first time from Dubai, and in five minutes he explained to me what he's doing in the most amazing way. And when I thought, who else, who of my network can explain what's optimization, I couldn't find more than Mohamed Soliman, Regional Vice President of Energy Exemplar, one of the leading companies in the optimization energy sector.

paragraphs.speaker: Eslam
paragraphs.text: So without further ado, Mohamed, welcome to the show.

paragraphs.text: Simple way is, and describe it, if you're faced to teach a young kid what that means, that means you don't understand it. So in my simple terms, I always start with those two points. If those A and B, one is higher than the other one. Is it better that you go from A to B or from B down to A, right? And this is just two points. Imagine if you have three points now.

paragraphs.text: Do you go from A to B to C, A, C, B, B, C, A, and so on? And this is where all the science and knowledge and experience behind comes to support those to this very simple question: how the best way to get from a point to another one.

paragraphs.text: I love that. I have to say, even thinking about going from two nodes to thousands of nodes, it just gave me a headache. paragraphs.text: Well, let's start again from the original concept, right? How we can simplify that, then we move it the machines that we are utilizing now can only understand ones and zeros. paragraphs.speaker: Mohamed
paragraphs.text: So I think the base is to have data, then to utilize the data and to transform the data into understandable form of like to machine, then apply the science on top of that and fundamentals in order to get to the optimization. paragraphs.speaker: Eslam
paragraphs.text: Love that. I would like to expand a bit more, and I would like to understand what types of decisions usually can these kind of algorithms help you as a leader to decide? paragraphs.text: Let's dive into the energy, for example. So when you talk about optimization, you actually need to define the objective of the optimization that you're running. paragraphs.speaker: Mohamed
paragraphs.text: So if we're talking about running a system, you need to reach the maximum benefit of the system while ensuring security of supply, while achieving minimum, let's say, emission, as well as also minimum cost. In this case, I know that you and I were discussing this earlier, where a consumer can be a producer at the same time, and this means the single node now becomes a load as well as a supplier. So this all comes under the same concept of the more sophisticated systems that we're running. And this is where optimization will have a different aspects and different angles. And this is where science becomes important.

paragraphs.speaker: Mohamed
paragraphs.text: Representation is one part of it. Defining the objective is another part of it. But also, you have a lot of variables to the system. This is where you move from deterministic statistics to more Monte Carlo or even stochastic, where you have a lot of variable that is changing randomly and you want to identify what is the best optimum point to operate the system based on all of those constraints, based on all of those representation of the system, as well as also the level of stochastics or statistics method that you're going to use.

paragraphs.text: Right. I love the way you kind of build the pyramid. paragraphs.text: Okay. And this always needs to come down to specific layers. As we just discussed, the data Now it becomes one of those foundation layer, right? So as they say, garbage in, garbage out. So that means first you need to identify the data validity and trustworthy of your data. And this is on its own is one of the exercises that you need to run, right? So the data accuracy and trustworthiness and also freshness and all of those, there is a lot of like keys to identify the data quality.

paragraphs.text: Right. This is the base. On top of that lies the foundation. What are you what are your objectives? What are the system constraints? A lot of things. So the methodology becomes the second layer to build this trust. So you have the foundation layer of data. Then you have the methodology. Then you have the governance, how you run that, because if we are talking about a lot of like optimization tools, then you have governance around what can be preached or not, what kind of constraints are strict or not. If you're using AI and a lot of, like, the recent, like, models and so on, then there can be some hallucinations, so how you can guardrail that and so on. Only then, when you have all of those trust layers, you can actually say that, all right, This is the model that I can trust. All right.

paragraphs.text: But without having those, first of all, foundation that you understand that the foundation is solid awareness, what type of foundation are running there? Right. It's not about the trust of the brand, the trust of of who's bringing you this intelligence or not. But it's all about having the right foundation in order to achieve that. That means you always challenge the models before you can really let your guards down where you can really get the model. But imagine that. If you choose not to trust any model, you're actually limiting yourself.

paragraphs.text: Because as we say in the sales-like domain, if you never ask, the answer will always be no. So imagine or consider the optimization is one of the tools that you may have that can provide you with some insights. You will be left behind if you're not utilizing the tools that are available now at your disposal. Imagine going to a war with a knife. paragraphs.text: So you need to be utilized with the right tools, set of tools.

paragraphs.text: Right, I love that. I love the way how you kind of layered out each layer to be able to, from foundations all the way up, to be able to trust the model and trust the outcomes. Well, let's narrow the question just

paragraphs.text: Like on an applicable level, let's say just for the energy now, right? How often the energy system change and how often do you need now the modeling to evolve, to adapt with those dynamics of the changes, right? You'd be surprised how dynamic it becomes, the energy model or the energy systems. Because in the past, you can say, right, I have, let's say, a power generation. I will turn it on. And considering the system, you will have some seasonality, but eventually let's assume that you have two seasons or day and night. But the numbers of variables becomes, I would say, it was simple. Imagine now that you are operating in a system where the speed of the wind decides the output of the generation.

paragraphs.text: It's a great question. And it's actually, this is where it's not just about the resilience versus the flexibility, but it also becomes the regulations becomes very crucial here. Because imagine if you are just talking about the flexibility and all of the generators, right, the companies, the GenCos decided that, all right, you know what, we'll just only generate in this high peak. That means you will have zero power actually away from this high prices or peak. So this is where becomes, right? This is where resilience becomes a crucial part. This is where regulations becomes crucial. This is where you need the steady loads, the steady generation. You need also to balance between the commercial benefits and the system resilience and security of supply. This will need to always be guided by governments who also use a modeling and optimization practice in a different scale, right? But this is again another optimization problem where you have the resilience and security of the systems versus the flexibility, and you need to find the optimum way between the two.

paragraphs.speaker: Mohamed
paragraphs.text: So in its own, to decide between the resilience and the flexibility is an optimization problem.

That means also you need to be aware of any limitation that you may have of the modeling aspects and tools and methodology that you're using. Because if you will need to wait a year for a resolution solution, based on your limited infrastructure, this becomes a deciding factor and so on. So it's also need to be a balance between the level of details that you need to achieve, and the level of infrastructure and technology availability that you have. This is where now becomes critical, the data centers, the computational powers, the flexibility of the technology and the availability of the technology becomes crucial.

paragraphs.speaker: Mohamed
paragraphs.text: And this is where all the global leaders are now racing towards that, because with more computational powers, you unlock actually a lot of optimization and insights in your data. And this is where you can get to better decisions that can worth billions of dollars and actually a lot of impact to a lot of lives.

paragraphs.text: That's fantastic. There's one term that I am not sure we related this to, something that I was reading is this kind of idea of what we call optimal optimization. And is that it's actually real, or is that just a kind of a fancy word or a marketing word that
